title: Research: prove four-site idle-rank rigidity under the fixed schedule
body:
**Scoped negative result.** Every operator-preserving replacement of idle children 8, 10, 12 and 13 in the fixed data schedule preserves each child's rank separately, under the inherited completed-call contract. This covers arbitrary simultaneous independent-axis replacements, including matched swaps and cycles. It answers the four-position question left open by #3196/#3199 without enumerating assignments. No new κ or supplier admission is claimed.

The proof has two steps. The intervening schedule preserves the receiver's two-dimensional coordinate subspace, so `E_B M E_A = M` forces both phase corrections to be identity. Polarization of a child's Z4 Fourier phase then recovers a binary matrix whose rank equals the number of independent axes. A complete phase signature uses 2,701 coefficients at dimension 73; this shortcut applies to individual child phases, not arbitrary circuit equality.

The checker authenticates the source schedule and all 448 full recipe bases across 112 ports. It does **not** reconstruct the T740 fill: rank 48 describes full recipe bases, while a hosted instance retains its own original residual ranks. Additional changed positions, changed intervening interactions and new local contracts are outside the theorem. Rank-preserving frame savings remain possible. Native execution and supplier/outer obligations are inherited, not reverified.

Reproduce:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/idle-four-site-rigidity
```

Expected: `PASS_IDLE_FOUR_SITE_RIGIDITY`, `PASS_IDLE_FOUR_SITE_EXPORT`, and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=negative-result`.

Registered Python 3.12.14 checks pass. Git-free optimized replay also passes on Python 3.14.7. Controls cover 1,447 small independent axis sets, 22,584 character evaluations, 8,192 phase tuples, five source-schedule mutations and three export/rejection cases. Positive controls demonstrate nontrivial equal-phase bases and a transfer after changing the invariant cut. All eleven committed package/input byte comparisons pass. The unrestricted statement rests on the written proof, not the finite replay; no proof-kernel or independent human review is claimed.

Base and refreshed main: `463113d675af7410ac91d53a4fed51ec6494eb9a`. Exact input/provenance pins are in `SOURCES.json`; scope, overlap, seed 40 and next questions are in `TASK.json`. Final overlap refresh covered 249 open PRs, 2,630 closed PRs and 2,004 Discussion records. #3200 involves additional positions and is outside this result.

Credit Gareth Davidson/#1387 and Nick Petalas/#3187 for the physical-stream obstruction and interval argument; Gonzalo-Mier/#3196/#3199 for the census and simultaneous-assignment question; Jeremy Diviney/#3148 and the retained word/geometry lineage. Ross Richardson's concurrent [handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2612#discussioncomment-18999338) reports a broader twenty-slot obstruction with local-only evidence. This submission supplies a separate, source-bound four-position proof and rank/phase representation; it claims neither exclusive priority nor review of that unpublished result.
